_schema_notes.purpose: Brand-specific tag evolution rules. Each signal is a dating anchor tied to a documented label design change, company event, or production shift. All dates are soft anchors unless marked hard_bound.
_schema_notes.confidence: high = well-documented, verifiable. medium = generally accepted, ±2-3 years. low = rough estimate, needs verification.
_schema_notes.todo: Expand with specific label photos and sub-variants as the dataset grows. Many medium/low entries here need refinement from real examples.

red_tab_big_E.description: Red pocket tab reads 'LEVI'S' with capital E throughout
red_tab_big_E.notes: Capital E in 'LEVI'S' on the red tab was changed to lowercase 'e' (appearing as 'LeVI'S') around 1971. Big E is one of the most reliable Levi's dating signals — definitively pre-1971.

red_tab_small_e.description: Red pocket tab reads 'LeVI'S' with lowercase e
red_tab_small_e.notes: Small e tab introduced ~1971. Post-1971 garment.

no_red_tab.description: No red tab present on back pocket
no_red_tab.notes: Levi's introduced the red tab in 1936 as a trademark identifier. Absence of a red tab predates this.

two_horse_leather_patch.description: Waistband patch made of genuine tan/brown leather
two_horse_leather_patch.notes: Original leather patch used through the early 1950s. Genuine leather patch strongly suggests pre-1955. Transition to simulated/cardstock was gradual.

two_horse_paper_cardstock_patch.description: Two-horse waistband patch made of cardstock or simulated leather
two_horse_paper_cardstock_patch.notes: Paper/cardstock patch replaced leather progressively from the mid-1950s. Exact transition year uncertain — flag for user verification.

hidden_rivets.description: Interior (hidden) crotch rivet — rivet on back pockets concealed inside, not visible externally
hidden_rivets.notes: Levi's used exposed copper rivets originally. In 1937 the crotch rivet was eliminated and back pocket rivets were moved inside (concealed) to prevent scratching saddles and furniture. Visible crotch rivet = pre-1937. Concealed back pocket rivets introduced 1937.

cinch_back.description: Cinch strap / buckle back on rear waistband
cinch_back.notes: Cinch backs were eliminated during WWII fabric rationing (1941-1942 era). Presence of a cinch back is a hard pre-1942 indicator.

suspender_buttons.description: Buttons on waistband interior for suspenders
suspender_buttons.notes: Suspender buttons were standard on jeans into the mid-20th century as belt loops coexisted with suspender culture. Presence suggests pre-1960 but is not definitive.

single_stitch.description: Single-needle stitching on seat seam and side seams
single_stitch.notes: Levi's transitioned from single to chain/double stitch in the early 1980s as production modernized. Single stitch on the outseam and seat seam is associated with pre-1983 production, though transition was gradual.

blue_bell_label.description: Label references 'Blue Bell' or Blue Bell branding
blue_bell_label.notes: Blue Bell Inc. was acquired by VF Corporation in 1986. Any label referencing Blue Bell is pre-acquisition.

wrangler_11mwz_label.notes: 11MWZ is a long-running style. Label design evolution within this style needs further documentation.

hd_lee_full_name.description: Label reads 'H.D. Lee Company' or 'H.D. Lee Mercantile Co.'
hd_lee_full_name.notes: Full H.D. Lee Company name on labels is associated with earlier production. By the early 1970s, branding had simplified to 'Lee'. Exact cutover year uncertain.

lee_riders.notes: Lee Riders was a specific western/cowboy-cut product line designation used through mid-century. Needs exact discontinuation date verification.

lee_union_alls.notes: Lee's Union-Alls (coveralls/overalls) product line. Associated with early-to-mid 20th century workwear production.

bar_tack_sleeve.description: Bar tack reinforcement stitch visible on upper left sleeve
bar_tack_sleeve.notes: Bar tack on the sleeve is associated with vintage Champion Reverse Weave production. Rough era — needs refinement from examples.

blue_bar_c_logo.description: Champion 'C' logo features blue bar/stripe through the letter
blue_bar_c_logo.notes: Blue stripe through the C logo is associated with 1970s-early 1990s Champion production. Logo styling changed multiple times — this era needs visual confirmation.

champion_made_usa.notes: Champion moved most production offshore by the late 1990s. Made in USA is strong evidence of pre-1998 production.

reverse_weave_label.notes: Reverse Weave as a named product line dates to 1938. Label design changes within this line need further documentation.

russell_made_usa.notes: Russell Athletic was based in Alexander City, Alabama and primarily domestic through the 20th century. Offshore shift accelerated in the early 2000s.

russell_jerzees_label.notes: Jerzees was introduced by Russell in 1984. Presence indicates post-1984.

pure_virgin_wool.description: Label reads '100% Pure Virgin Wool' or 'Pure Wool'
pure_virgin_wool.notes: The 'Pure Virgin Wool' label copy is associated with Pendleton's mid-century production. Later labels added more content detail and regulatory fiber disclosure language.

made_in_oregon.description: Label reads 'Made in Oregon' or lists an Oregon mill
made_in_oregon.notes: Pendleton's Oregon mills were active through the 20th century. The specific Oregon callout is more common on older labels.

carhartt_made_usa.notes: Carhartt shifted significant production offshore in the late 1990s-early 2000s. Made in USA Carhartt is strongly pre-2000. Some USA production continued post-2000 on select lines.

carhartt_union_label.description: Carhartt garment bears ACWA, ACTWU, or ILGWU union label
carhartt_union_label.notes: Union label presence applies union existence hard bounds. Carhartt workwear was frequently union-made through the mid-20th century.

fotl_made_usa.notes: Fruit of the Loom closed its last US plant in 1998. Made in USA is a hard indicator of pre-1998.

fotl_screen_stars.description: Label reads 'Screen Stars' (FOTL's blank T-shirt line)
fotl_screen_stars.notes: Screen Stars was FOTL's premium blank line, popular with screenprinters. The specific era of Screen Stars needs sub-design documentation.

Hanes.official_name: Hanesbrands Inc. (formerly Sara Lee Knit Products)

hanes_made_usa.notes: Hanes shifted offshore significantly in the late 1990s. Made in USA is strongly pre-2000.

sara_lee_era.description: Label or brand materials reference Sara Lee Corporation
sara_lee_era.notes: Sara Lee Corporation acquired Hanes in 1979. Sara Lee spun off its apparel brands in 2006 as Hanesbrands Inc.

polo_founding_bound.notes: Ralph Lauren brand did not exist before 1967. Any Polo/Ralph Lauren label is post-1967.

polo_made_usa.notes: Polo produced more domestically in its earlier decades. Made in USA Polo suggests earlier production, generally pre-1995.

founding_bound.notes: Tommy Hilfiger brand did not exist before 1985.
Nautica brand did not exist before 1983.
Calvin Klein brand did not exist before 1968.

ck_jeans_label.notes: Calvin Klein Jeans launched ~1978. Presence suggests post-1978.

Members_Only.official_name: Members Only (Glenoit Mills / Europe Craft Imports)

peak_era.description: Members Only brand jacket or garment
peak_era.notes: Members Only jackets had their cultural peak in the early-to-mid 1980s. The brand faded significantly post-1990. A Members Only garment is most likely 1980-1990, though the brand technically continues.
